issues.title: Empty lines not filtered in Expected Events textarea
issues.description: In the CustomTriggerFields component, the onChange handler for the Expected Events textarea fails to filter out empty or whitespace-only lines. When users press Enter multiple times or leave blank lines between events, these empty strings are included in the events array sent to the trigger configuration. This will cause backend validation failures or create malformed automation triggers that expect empty event names, leading to automations that never fire correctly.

issues.title: Incorrect field switching in DeploymentStatusTriggerFields breaks trigger data model
issues.description: The DeploymentStatusTriggerFields component incorrectly implements posture-dependent field switching, using 'trigger.after' for Proactive posture and 'trigger.expect' for Reactive posture. While this pattern exists in FlowRunStateTriggerFields where it serves a semantic purpose (states to enter vs. stay in), deployment status triggers don't have this distinction in the backend data model. This causes the selected status to be written to the wrong field when Proactive posture is selected, potentially causing data loss when the form is saved or incorrect trigger behavior. The backend may not recognize 'after' field for deployment status events.

issues.title: parseInt without radix causes NaN values in threshold field
issues.description: In WorkPoolStatusTriggerFields, the threshold input's onChange handler uses `parseInt(e.target.value)` without specifying a radix parameter. When users clear the threshold field, parseInt returns NaN instead of a number, which gets set as the form value. This breaks form validation and can cause runtime errors when the automation is saved. Additionally, parseInt will silently truncate decimal inputs (e.g., 1.5 becomes 1) rather than properly handling invalid input, and without the radix parameter it may misinterpret values with leading zeros as octal numbers in older JavaScript environments.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #19997 - feat(ui-v2): Add trigger form templates
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR replaces the four "coming soon" placeholders in the automations trigger step with real form components: deployment status, work pool status, work queue status, and custom. Each one reuses the posture select, threshold, and conditional "Within (seconds)" pattern from FlowRunStateTriggerFields. The status event strings I checked against the server match what it emits (`prefect.<resource>.{status.in_kebab_case()}` for READY, NOT_READY, and PAUSED). The PR also quietly flips `strict` to false in `ui-v2/tsconfig.app.json`, which affects the whole app and is not mentioned in the description.

The main problems are in the wiring, not the event names. The work pool and work queue components always write to `trigger.expect`, while the deployment-status and flow-run-state components write to `trigger.after` for Proactive triggers. That breaks the "same pattern" the PR claims to follow. The custom textarea has a dead `lines.length > 0 ? lines : undefined` branch, so an empty box stores `[""]`. The tests also only check posture and threshold, which are shared across all templates, so they would still pass if the status select or the field switch were broken.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `strict: false` change disables type checking across the entire UI and is unrelated to the feature. The Proactive field mismatch means work pool and work queue status triggers will behave differently from deployment status triggers. Both should be fixed before merge. The custom textarea empty-state bug and the weak tests should also be addressed. The event name strings are correct.

architecture.overview:
The automations wizard is a react-hook-form + zod form. `AutomationWizard` owns the form with `AutomationWizardSchema` as its resolver and defaults `trigger` to a Reactive event trigger. `TriggerStep` renders a template picker and then a `TriggerTemplateFields` switch that picks one field component per template. Every trigger field component writes into the shared `trigger.*` keys: `expect` and `after` (string arrays), `threshold`, `within`, and `posture`. The wizard's submit handler currently only logs the values, so the schema is the only contract in play today.

This PR adds four components (deployment status, work pool status, work queue status, custom) and swaps them into the switch in place of placeholder text. Status components use a single-select that writes a one-element array. The custom component uses a textarea that splits on newlines. The Reactive/Proactive switch decides which array key a field writes to. The event names written by the status selects have to match the strings the server emits from `models/events.py`.
steps: Entry point: `AutomationWizard` (`automation-wizard.tsx`) builds the form and defaults `trigger` to `{posture: "Reactive", threshold: 1, within: 0}`. `TriggerStep` renders the template select, then `TriggerTemplateFields` switches on the chosen template.

Pre-existing pattern: `FlowRunStateTriggerFields` picks `trigger.after` for Proactive and `trigger.expect` for Reactive, and shares `PostureSelect`, threshold, and the conditional within field. This PR's deployment-status component copies that switch, but the work pool and work queue components do not.

New status components: each one renders a Select whose options are hard-coded `prefect.<resource>.<status>` strings, and writes `[value]` into the field. The deployment-status, work-pool, and work-queue option sets match the server's READY, NOT_READY, and PAUSED enums.
New custom component: a textarea is bound to `trigger.expect`. Each change splits the text on `\n` and writes the array back. Blank lines and an empty box both become `[""]` entries.
Tooling change: `tsconfig.app.json` sets `strict` to false for the whole `src` tree. The type checker's null and implicit-any checks are off for every file in the app, not just these new ones.

findings.title: Global `strict: false` added to the app's tsconfig
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/tsconfig.app.json` (line 19), revert `"strict": false` back to `"strict": true`. Then run `tsc -b` in `ui-v2`. For any new strict-mode errors in the trigger-step components (`trigger-step/*-trigger-fields.tsx`), fix them locally with proper types or guards, such as handling `field.value` possibly being undefined. Do not change the project-wide compiler setting.

findings.title: Work pool and work queue status triggers ignore Proactive `after` semantics
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/`, `work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx` (around line 36) and `work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx` (around line 36) always bind the status field to `trigger.expect`. Change them to use the same posture switch as `deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx` (lines 29-31) and `flow-run-state-trigger-fields.tsx` (lines 22-25): `trigger.after` when posture is Proactive, `trigger.expect` otherwise. Also make the Proactive/Reactive label consistent with those files. Add a test that checks the status value is written to `after` when posture is Proactive.

findings.title: Custom textarea stores `[""]` for empty input; the `undefined` branch is dead code
findings.body:
`String.prototype.split` always returns at least one element, so `lines.length > 0` is always true and the `undefined` branch never runs. Clearing the box therefore stores `[""]` instead of an empty or unset array. Blank lines and trailing whitespace are also kept as separate entries.

The rendered value round-trips (`[""].join("\n")` is `""`), so the UI looks correct, which is why the bug is easy to miss. The stored value is wrong, though. Empty strings are not meaningful event names, and the server builds its matching pattern from these values. The schema (`expect: z.array(z.string())`) accepts `[""]`, so validation will not catch it.

::code{file="ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/custom-trigger-fields.tsx" lines="34-42"}

The PR asked reviewers to verify this conversion. It needs a fix: trim each line, drop empty ones, and store `undefined` when nothing is left.
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/custom-trigger-fields.tsx`, the textarea `onChange` (around lines 37-40) splits on `\n` and then checks `lines.length > 0`, which is always true, so an empty box stores `[""]`. Change it to split, trim each line, and filter out empty entries. Then store the array if it has items, or `undefined` if it is empty. Keep the `value={events.join("\n")}` display as is. Add a unit test covering empty input, blank lines between entries, and surrounding whitespace.

findings.title: Tests only check the shared fields, so the new status and custom logic is untested
findings.body:
Each new template test in `trigger-step.test.tsx` checks only `select posture` and `Threshold` (and for custom, the textarea label). Those controls come from the shared `PostureSelect` and the threshold field, which are rendered by every template. The tests would still pass if the status select were missing, if the options were wrong, if a status value were written to the wrong key, or if the Proactive field switch were broken.

Nothing checks any of these:
- the status select renders and offers the expected options,
- selecting a status stores a single-element array,
- Proactive writes to `after` and Reactive writes to `expect`,
- the custom textarea round-trips and handles empty input.

Flow-run-state has its own `*.test.tsx` file that covers its specific behavior. These components have no such file.

::diff{file="ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/trigger-step.test.tsx" lines="45-56"}

Add per-component tests modelled on `flow-run-state-trigger-fields.test.tsx` that assert on the form's stored values, not only on the presence of shared fields.
findings.fixPrompt: The new template tests in `ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/trigger-step.test.tsx` (lines 45-111) only assert the shared `select posture`, `Threshold`, and custom textarea labels. Add per-component test files for `deployment-status`, `work-pool-status`, `work-queue-status`, and `custom` trigger fields, modelled on `flow-run-state-trigger-fields.test.tsx`. Each should cover: the status select options, that a status selection is stored as a one-element array, that Proactive writes to `trigger.after` while Reactive writes to `trigger.expect`, that the within field appears only for Proactive, and (for custom) the textarea conversion including empty input. Assert on the form values, not just that elements render.

findings.title: Four status components duplicate the same form block
findings.body:
`deployment-status`, `work-pool-status`, and `work-queue-status` are close to identical. The only real differences are the option list and, in one case, the field-name switch. The posture select, threshold field, and conditional within field are repeated in all five trigger field files. This duplication is the reason the work pool and work queue components drifted from the deployment component on the Proactive field, and it will drift again the next time one is edited.

A shared `StatusTriggerFields` component that takes the option list and owns the posture-to-field switch would remove most of the copies and make that behavior consistent.

::code{file="ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx" lines="29-58"}

This is a maintainability concern, not a bug, so it can wait if you want to ship the fixes above first.
findings.fixPrompt: The files `deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx`, `work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx`, and `work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx` in `ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/` duplicate the same posture select, status select, threshold field, and conditional within field. Extract a shared `StatusTriggerFields` component that takes the status option list as a prop and owns the posture-based field switch (`trigger.after` for Proactive, `trigger.expect` otherwise). Have the three status components become thin wrappers that pass their option list. Keep the exported component names and `index.ts` exports unchanged so callers don't change.

findings.title: Status select has no accessible name
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx`, `work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx`, and `work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx`, the `SelectTrigger` for the status select (around line 50 in the deployment file) has no `aria-label`. Add `aria-label="select status"` to each, following the `aria-label="select posture"` pattern in `posture-select.tsx`. Then add a test that finds the status select by that label.

findings.title: Work pool threshold uses `parseInt` without a radix and differs from its siblings
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx`, the threshold `onChange` (around line 78) uses `parseInt(e.target.value)`. Change it to `Number(e.target.value)` to match the threshold field in `deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx` and the within fields in the other components.

findings.title: Status event names match the server's emitted events
findings.body:
I checked the hard-coded event strings against the server. `models/events.py` emits `prefect.deployment.{status.in_kebab_case()}`, `prefect.work-pool.{...}`, and `prefect.work-queue.{...}`. `in_kebab_case()` lowercases the enum value and replaces `_` with `-`. The server enums include READY, NOT_READY, and PAUSED for work pools and work queues, and READY and NOT_READY for deployments. So `prefect.deployment.ready`, `prefect.deployment.not-ready`, `prefect.work-pool.{ready,not-ready,paused}`, and `prefect.work-queue.{ready,not-ready,paused}` are all correct. Deployments correctly have no Paused option.

::code{file="ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx" lines="20-24"}

findings.title: Placeholder tests were replaced with assertions on the real components
findings.body: The old tests asserted that the placeholder text was visible. The updated tests drop those assertions and check for the shared posture select and threshold instead. That fails loudly if the placeholder comes back, and it confirms each template renders its fields. The assertions are still shallow, as noted in the test-coverage finding above. Still, the test names now match what is tested, and the `index.ts` barrel exports stay in alphabetical order.

findings.title: Within field defaulting and Proactive gating follow the existing pattern
findings.body: Each new component shows the `Within (seconds)` field only when `posture === "Proactive"`, using the same `useWatch` gate as `FlowRunStateTriggerFields`. `PostureSelect` still sets the default within value (30) when the user switches to Proactive, so the new components inherit that behavior without extra code. Status triggers store one-element arrays, which matches the review focus.
